QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_39

question.text: What is a 'Liquidation Scheme' as defined in the SEBI (AIF) framework?

answer.text: A Cat III scheme launched to pursue long-short strategies during market downturns.
A close-ended AIF scheme launched only for the purpose of liquidating the unliquidated investments in an existing AIF scheme whose tenure has expired.
A liquidation advisory service offered by merchant bankers, not an AIF scheme.
A separate liquidation fund run by the trustee after Manager termination.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12: 'Liquidation Scheme means a close-ended AIF scheme launched only for the purpose of liquidating the unliquidated investments in its existing AIF scheme, whose tenure has expired.' Note: post April 25, 2024, no new Liquidation Schemes can be launched. The Trap: Option A is a Cat III strategy (long-short) and is not a Liquidation Scheme. Options C and D invent roles. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same definition. The 2024 shutdown rule makes this a historical concept — still testable for definition. Manager's Pro-Tip: Because Liquidation Schemes are closed post-2024, you should understand them CONCEPTUALLY (for comparison with in-specie and Dissolution Period) but will not launch one — plan the Dissolution Period route instead.
